aMcJ1Jvtef0.summary: Mark Ferrari, the LucasArts background artist, explains in a GDC 2016 talk how he draws 8-bit graphics. He covers color cycling and palette shifting to create complex animated scenery without frame animation.
aMcJ1Jvtef0.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as a master class in limited-palette pixel art and palette cycling, from an artist behind Loom and Monkey Island.

aircAruvnKk.summary: 3Blue1Brown's first chapter on deep learning explains what neurons and layers are and the math underlying a basic neural network, using handwritten digit recognition with visual animations.
aircAruvnKk.why: HN treats it as the standard first stop for learning neural networks, praised for making the math intuitive.

aVwxzDHniEw.summary: Freya Holmer explains how Bezier curves work, from the helper-line construction to their uses in animation, text rendering and shapes. It uses visuals from her Unity Shapes plugin and was a SoME1 contest winner.
aVwxzDHniEw.why: HN repeatedly calls it one of the best math and graphics explainers on YouTube, praised for bridging game dev and math.

ar9WRwCiSr0.summary: Tom Murphy (suckerpinch) shows 'reverse emulation', using a Raspberry Pi in an NES cartridge to give an unmodified NES new abilities such as playing SNES games. The video starts in a strange way and gets stranger.
ar9WRwCiSr0.why: Praised as a brilliant, deadpan and inventive hardware hack, and a good starting point for Tom7's videos.

aAb7hSCtvGw.summary: Joshua Bloch's Google Tech Talk on how to design good APIs and why it matters, with concrete principles and examples. It treats every programmer as an occasional API designer.
aAb7hSCtvGw.why: HN repeatedly names it the best resource on API design, a staple answer to any 'how do I design an API' question.

a9xAKttWgP4.summary: A short Dyalog demonstration building Conway's Game of Life in a single line of APL, step by step. It shows how array operations replace loops.
a9xAKttWgP4.why: Recommended whenever APL or array languages come up as the quickest way to see why the paradigm is so striking.

ajGX7odA87k.summary: James Mickens's humorous USENIX Security keynote argues that improving security and trusting opaque technology like machine learning is far harder than the industry admits.
ajGX7odA87k.why: HN considers it a classic, hilarious and sobering talk on ML inscrutability and tech hubris, often rewatched.

a1zDuOPkMSw.summary: Richard Hamming's 1995 recording of his talk 'You and Your Research', drawn from his graduate engineering course. He discusses how great scientists pick important problems and build careers, drawing on his years at Bell Labs.
a1zDuOPkMSw.why: HN recommends it as career and research advice on choosing important problems and doing first-class work.

aKLntZcp27M.summary: Catherine West's RustConf 2018 closing keynote on building a game in Rust and organizing a large codebase. It builds up an entity component system and generational indices step by step.
aKLntZcp27M.why: HN treats it as the go-to explanation of ECS, valuable even for people who don't use Rust.

akVL7QY0S8A.summary: Elizabeth Warren's 2007 Berkeley lecture, when she was a Harvard law professor, on why middle-class families are under growing financial strain. She draws on bankruptcy research to examine rising costs of housing, health care and education.
akVL7QY0S8A.why: HN cites it often in debates on inequality, cost disease and stagnant middle-class income, praising its data-driven approach.

a-BOSpxYJ9M.summary: Dave Thomas, a co-author of the Agile Manifesto, argues at GOTO Amsterdam 2015 that Agile as a branded industry has lost its meaning. He says agile is an adjective, not a noun, and urges developers to reclaim agility.
a-BOSpxYJ9M.why: Offered in nearly every Agile or Scrum complaint thread as the authoritative take on what agile was meant to be versus what it became.

agZ0xISi40E.summary: CGP Grey's six-minute explainer of the relationships the UK could have with the EU, based on Barnier's slide, shown as orbits of different closeness. It explains why the UK's red lines ruled out the closer options.
agZ0xISi40E.why: HN recommends it as the quickest clear overview of the Brexit options, though later commenters note it predates the final outcome.

atvtBE6t48M.summary: Dean Friedman's near-hour-long introduction to synthesis, covering the building blocks of sound and the controls on a synthesizer. He slowly adjusts knobs so viewers hear what each parameter does.
atvtBE6t48M.why: Repeatedly called the best beginner course on audio synthesis, since the concepts have not changed since it was made.

a0atL1HSwi8.summary: Official trailer for Eugene Jarecki's 2012 documentary The House I Live In, an investigative look at America's war on drugs and its effect on the criminal justice system. It won the Grand Jury Prize at Sundance.
a0atL1HSwi8.why: HN commenters recommend the film itself as an eye-opening account of how drug laws drove mass incarceration and militarized policing.

aFwVf5a3pZM.summary: Larry McEnerney of the University of Chicago Writing Program argues that good writing is defined by what readers value, not by rules or the writer's own ideas. He explains why academic habits fail outside academia and how to write so readers find the work valuable.
aFwVf5a3pZM.why: HN treats it as the definitive writing lecture and recommends it repeatedly, with several commenters saying it changed how they write.

aB8zcAttP1E.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Navy pilot David Fravor, a primary witness of the 2004 Tic Tac UFO encounter, about the sighting, military aviation and aerospace engineering. The conversation runs close to four hours.
aB8zcAttP1E.why: HN commenters send people here for a detailed first-hand account from the pilot, and some say it changed their view on the sightings.

aSEQfqNYNAc.summary: A five-minute excerpt of Rich Hickey's Clojure Made Simple talk, with new slides, ranting about HttpServletRequest and specificity. He argues for using generic maps instead of many specific classes and getters.
aSEQfqNYNAc.why: Cited as the classic rant on maps versus objects in discussions of data modeling and OOP.

agOdP2Bmieg.summary: Bret Victor's closing keynote at UIST and SPLASH 2014 argues that our tools for thinking ignore most of human sensory and motor capability. He sketches representations that engage more modalities beyond screens and keyboards.
agOdP2Bmieg.why: HN treats it as a foundational Bret Victor talk that reshaped how people think about software and interfaces, often cited alongside Dynamicland.

aFQFB5YpDZE.summary: Jon Stewart appears as a guest on CNN's Crossfire in 2004 and criticizes hosts Tucker Carlson and Paul Begala for turning political debate into partisan theater that hurts America.
aFQFB5YpDZE.why: HN returns to it constantly as the definitive critique of adversarial TV punditry, still seen as relevant to polarized media and online discourse.

aMcjxSThD54.summary: Channel 4 News's full interview with Jordan Peterson, in which Cathy Newman presses him on the gender pay gap, patriarchy, campus protests and postmodernism. It was widely discussed for its confrontational style.
aMcjxSThD54.why: HN cites it as the classic example of an interviewer misrepresenting a guest, though opinions on who came out better differ.

arj7oStGLkU.summary: Tim Urban's TED talk on why people procrastinate, covering YouTube binges and Wikipedia rabbit holes. It ends with the life-calendar idea as a nudge to act before time runs out.
arj7oStGLkU.why: Recommended as a funny, empathetic take on procrastination and the origin of the life calendar concept.

ainyK6fXku0.summary: William Shatner's spoken-word cover of Pulp's 'Common People', from his album Has Been.
ainyK6fXku0.why: HN commenters repeatedly recommend it as a surprisingly good cover that brings out the contempt in the lyrics.

aDejwCGdUV8.summary: A three-hour Joe Rogan Experience conversation with Graham Hancock and Randall Carlson about lost civilizations, the Younger Dryas impact hypothesis and Earth's cataclysmic history.
aDejwCGdUV8.why: HN people point to it as an entry point to the Hancock and Carlson lost-civilization theories, while noting the ideas are controversial.

aHun58mz3vI.summary: A short satirical segment from Charlie Brooker's Newswipe that lampoons the formulaic conventions of television news reporting, from stock shots to filler street interviews and news-speak.
aHun58mz3vI.why: HN invokes it as the best spoof of how news is formulaically produced, often when discussing media quality or automated news.

aO3JgPUJ6iQ.summary: Captain Disillusion debunks a viral Chinese invisibility cloak video while parodying popular educational channels. Along the way he explains chroma keying and green screen techniques.
aO3JgPUJ6iQ.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining explanation of chroma keying, green screens and how cameras process color.

ab-r0capbzk.summary: Science journalist potholer54 examines the claim that SARS-CoV-2 came from a Wuhan lab, tracing the sources behind it and the weaknesses in the evidence.
ab-r0capbzk.why: HN commenters recommend it as a methodical debunking of early lab-leak claims.

amJ-ev8Ial8.summary: Joseph Everett argues, drawing on the book The Salt Fix, that most people benefit from more rather than less salt, and reviews studies on sodium, potassium and blood pressure.
amJ-ev8Ial8.why: HN commenters use it as a source of study references suggesting standard low-salt advice may be too restrictive.

ax7f3JZJHSw.summary: Razbuten has his wife, who has never played games, try a sampling of titles and shows where she struggles. It highlights unspoken game conventions that experienced players take for granted.
ax7f3JZJHSw.why: HN uses it to illustrate learned literacy in game and software UX, and how unfamiliar conventions confuse newcomers.

agzNANfNlTs.summary: Innuendo Studios' Alt-Right Playbook episode, drawing on Corey Robin's The Reactionary Mind, argues that conservatism defends hierarchy and a shrinking in-group.
agzNANfNlTs.why: Cited as a thoughtful video essay and for its model of in-group hierarchy in political threads.

an5abNFba4Q.summary: Jack Moffitt presents the architecture of Servo, Mozilla's experimental browser engine written in Rust, focusing on parallelism across cores, GPUs and SIMD and the safety properties gained from Rust.
an5abNFba4Q.why: HN recommends it as an exciting look at how a browser can be rebuilt for performance and safety, including the WebRender ideas that fed into Firefox Quantum.

aoczYXJeMY4.summary: The Thought Emporium's update on the home-brewed gene therapy he took to cure his lactose intolerance. It reports how the effect held up over two years and what future versions might look like.
aoczYXJeMY4.why: Pointed to as a striking example of DIY biology and self-experimentation with gene therapy.

a9b9IYqsb_U.summary: A HOPE conference talk by Howard Payne and Deviant Ollam on common keys, such as elevator and fire service keys, that open many buildings. It covers physical security weaknesses from shared key standards.
a9b9IYqsb_U.why: Brought up in threads on elevators and locks as an engaging talk on common keys.

aICaAEXDJQQ.summary: Real Engineering explains the engineering behind the James Webb Space Telescope, including its folding mirror, sunshield, orbit and cooling systems, and why deployment was so difficult.
aICaAEXDJQQ.why: HN recommends it as an accessible in-depth explanation of how Webb works and why its deployment was remarkable.

aIx2N-viNwY.summary: Veritasium explores why time seems to speed up as we age, covering chronoception and several competing explanations beyond the common proportional-theory argument.
aIx2N-viNwY.why: Cited in threads about perceived time as a good, detailed explanation of the effect.

aP0Y1uAA-2Y.summary: John Gustafson presents posits, a proposed drop-in replacement for IEEE 754 floats that is simpler in hardware and more flexible in precision. The seminar includes a live demo and machine learning results.
aP0Y1uAA-2Y.why: Cited in floating-point threads as the main introduction to posits and unums as an alternative to IEEE floats.

aVUqaB0IMh4.summary: A 100-minute tutorial from Phil's Lab on designing an STM32-based 'black pill' PCB in KiCad 6. It covers schematic capture, two-layer layout and routing, USB, and sending the board for manufacture and assembly.
aVUqaB0IMh4.why: HN recommends it as a practical way to learn KiCad and PCB design by following one full project.

aXQ2lO3ieBA.summary: A roughly ten-minute scene from the movie The Pentagon Wars showing how the Bradley Fighting Vehicle's requirements ballooned through committee demands into a compromised design. It is a satirical dramatization of military procurement.
aXQ2lO3ieBA.why: Linked in nearly every F-35 or procurement thread as the classic illustration of feature creep and design by stakeholder committee, including in software.

aXflBZXAucQ.summary: Berkeley sleep scientist Matthew Walker presents the science of sleep and dreams and how sleep affects health and lifespan, based on his book Why We Sleep.
aXflBZXAucQ.why: HN suggests it as an easy alternative to the book for people who want Walker's sleep findings.

aY985qzn7oI.summary: Physicist Angela Collier gives an hour-long critique of Avi Loeb's alien claims and reputation, placing them within the broader topic of physics crackpots. The Loeb discussion starts around the 24 minute mark.
aY985qzn7oI.why: Frequently linked as an in-depth, well-presented skeptical take whenever Loeb's alien claims come up.

agS6ZXBrcng.summary: A 1983 behind-the-scenes film about making the HBO 'Feature Presentation' starship logo sequence. It shows the handcrafted miniature city, motion-control cameras and practical effects.
agS6ZXBrcng.why: HN recommends it as a look at pre-CGI effects work that looks like CGI but was entirely physical.

a1PtQ67urG4.summary: David Spiegelhalter, Professor of the Public Understanding of Risk, uses statistics to weigh everyday risks such as bacon sandwiches and cycling. The six-minute piece introduces micromorts as a way to compare the risk of dying.
a1PtQ67urG4.why: Recommended as a short, fun introduction to micromorts and thinking about risk.

aNAtbYSxzuA.summary: Jonathan Schiefer interviews Larry Wall, creator of Perl, in a 33-minute conversation. Wall discusses his self-designed linguistics degree and how language and programming overlap.
aNAtbYSxzuA.why: Recommended as an enjoyable look at the hacker mindset and a thoughtful interview worth rewatching.

aXvDEmo6uS4.summary: A long Huberman Lab episode laying out science-based daily tools for focus, sleep, exercise and mental and physical health, organized around a 24-hour day.
aXvDEmo6uS4.why: Commenters credit it for practical routines, such as morning walks and circadian timing, and for helping with burnout recovery.

aZY-yQYVf38.summary: The 1985 Channel 4 TV film 'Max Headroom: 20 Minutes into the Future', the origin of the computer-generated TV host Max Headroom, with a soundtrack by Midge Ure and Chris Cross.
aZY-yQYVf38.why: Recommended in Max Headroom threads as a surprisingly good, short original film.

aeRVdYN6fE8.summary: Philip Wadler's Lambda Days talk on propositions as types, the link between logic and computation that underlies theorem provers and programming language design.
aeRVdYN6fE8.why: Recommended as an exceptional whirlwind tour of the foundations of computer science.

agw-wlHGi0E.summary: A 2001 panel with Paul Graham, John Maeda, Jonathan Rees and Guy Steele on programming language design, part of the Dynamic Languages Wizards Series.
agw-wlHGi0E.why: HN users mine it for design wisdom and history from luminaries, and often quote Guy Steele's remarks.

a1rC79DHpmY.summary: Max Brunsfeld of GitHub presents Tree-sitter, a parsing system for programming tools that supports incremental, error-tolerant parsing. He demos its integration into GitHub.com and Atom for syntax highlighting and code navigation.
a1rC79DHpmY.why: Recommended as the canonical introduction to tree-sitter and why fast incremental parsing enables live editor support.

aBBuoD9eL5k.summary: Jacob Geller's video essay on empty cities and what they say about our relationship to places, using games, literature and aerial imagery. It touches on works such as Invisible Cities.
aBBuoD9eL5k.why: HN points to Geller's essays as accessible companions to literary works and as a good summary of a story.

aCv10_WvGxo.summary: An Adam Ruins Everything segment arguing that purebred dogs suffer from inbreeding and genetic disorders, and that mutts are healthier. It follows the show's comedic debunking style.
aCv10_WvGxo.why: Shared in dog-breeding threads as a snappy summary of the genetic-diversity problem.

aDMjgOYOcDw.summary: An hour-plus Some More News episode that critiques Ben Shapiro's arguments and record of errors. It is a long, comedic and opinionated breakdown.
aDMjgOYOcDw.why: Occasionally recommended as an in-depth critical take on Shapiro, though mentions are sparse and partisan.

aDNPhq5ggoE.summary: A short NIST-based demonstration places a room furnished with old natural-material furniture beside one with modern synthetic furnishings and burns both. The modern room reaches full flashover in a few minutes while the legacy room is only starting to spread.
aDNPhq5ggoE.why: HN uses it as vivid proof that modern fires develop much faster, which is the argument for working smoke detectors and early escape.

aHx-XUA6f9g.summary: Ken Shirriff walks through how to reverse engineer integrated circuits from die photos, using famous chips as examples, in a Hackaday SuperConference talk.
aHx-XUA6f9g.why: Recommended as a clear account of the craft of reading chips from photographs.

aIHj3qMRqqE.summary: Kenneth Finnegan shows how USB-C Power Delivery trigger boards like the ZY12PDN negotiate 5V to 20V so you can power projects from a USB-C charger, including the color coding for each voltage.
aIHj3qMRqqE.why: Recommended as a practical way to get 12V or other voltages from USB-C for hobby projects.

aMnn0Jq0J-E.summary: Jon Bentley walks through three implementations of Hoare's Quicksort, from a dozen-line C function to a series of systematic code transformations that make the program ever simpler and more powerful. It is a Google Tech Talk on code elegance and program derivation.
aMnn0Jq0J-E.why: HN commenters point to it as programming inspiration and as a source of Bentley's anecdotes about adding function by deleting code.

aNR4n0i2ZlM.summary: Inigo Quilez shows step by step how to build a simple heart shape from mathematics and shaders, with code on Shadertoy. It is an introduction to procedural graphics and signed distance functions.
aNR4n0i2ZlM.why: HN commenters call it a great beginner-friendly introduction and enjoy watching Quilez work through graphics.

aT7mnSstKGs.summary: Artem Dinaburg's DEF CON 19 talk on bit-squatting, where flipped bits in DRAM cause devices to contact domains that differ by one bit from legitimate ones. He shows how registering such domains can hijack traffic without exploiting any software bug.
aT7mnSstKGs.why: HN cites it in ECC memory debates and bit-flip discussions as concrete evidence that memory errors have real security consequences.

aWvHrih-Juk.summary: Everyday Astronaut's guide to visiting Starbase, Texas to see Starship, covering what and where it is, which areas close during launches, where to watch from, where to fly into and stay, and things to do.
aWvHrih-Juk.why: Recommended as the practical guide for anyone planning to attend a Starship launch in person.

aeWyp2vXxqA.summary: Kurzgesagt explains black hole stars, a hypothesized kind of giant star with a black hole at its core that could be a route to early supermassive black holes.
aeWyp2vXxqA.why: HN uses it as a quick, accessible introduction to the black hole star concept in threads about early-universe black holes.

aiv1JOfMjm0.summary: Rick Hudson's GopherCon 2015 talk on Go 1.5's new low-latency concurrent garbage collector. It covers the motivation, performance numbers, technical challenges and why the approach fits Go.
aiv1JOfMjm0.why: Pointed to as the authoritative source on Go's GC pause improvements, and later revisited when GC latency claims were challenged.

alasBxZsb40.summary: Mike Wallace interviews Aldous Huxley in 1958 about the warnings in Brave New World, including mass persuasion, overpopulation and voluntary totalitarianism.
alasBxZsb40.why: Recommended as more thought-provoking than the usual pill-popping take on Huxley.

ao2GL3NAWQU.summary: Social psychologist Melanie Joy introduces the concept of carnism, the belief system that conditions people to eat some animals but not others.
ao2GL3NAWQU.why: HN offers it as a short, light introduction to carnism and the language bias around eating animals.

aoNOVlxJmow.summary: Mentour Pilot, a 737 captain, demonstrates in a full flight simulator why a Boeing 737 can become impossible to trim manually at high speed. He explains the jackscrew forces and the roller-coaster manoeuvre.
aoNOVlxJmow.why: HN pointed to it during the 737 MAX discussions to show how hard manual trim is when severely out of trim.

aokNwKx7gM8.summary: Matt Parker of Stand-up Maths examines scatter plots that were claimed to show fraudulent vote-switching in Michigan's 2020 election. He recreates the analysis and shows that the pattern arises from comparing percentages across different bases, not from fraud.
aokNwKx7gM8.why: HN commenters cite it as a clear debunking of election-fraud statistics and as a warning against comparing percentages without context.

aoy_WJ3mE50.summary: Tom Scott visits Onkalo in Finland, the planned deep geologic repository for high-level nuclear waste intended to be sealed for 100,000 years.
aoy_WJ3mE50.why: Recommended in nuclear waste threads as a short, clear look at a real long-term storage solution.

au0QJYISe4c.summary: ScienceClic explains why nothing can go faster than light by treating motion through space and time together, so everything moves at the speed of light through spacetime. It uses animated visuals to cover relativity basics in 12 minutes.
au0QJYISe4c.why: HN commenters recommend it as a helpful way to conceptualize why light speed is a limit.

aw7fUMhNov8.summary: This Old House's Ross Trethewey explains MERV filter ratings and how air filtration works, then shows how to build a localized DIY air filter, including a box fan with multiple filters.
aw7fUMhNov8.why: HN recommends it as a practical breakdown of filtration versus air volume and a clever box-fan filter design.

azI3nqrHEXM.summary: All Cars with Jon explains how EPA fuel economy rules, especially the footprint-based CAFE formula, push automakers away from small trucks.
azI3nqrHEXM.why: Cited in threads on vehicle bloat as the explanation for why small pickups disappeared in the US.

aAlR3cezPJg.summary: Lecture 7A from MIT 6.001 (SICP) by Abelson and Sussman introduces the metacircular evaluator, a Scheme interpreter written in Scheme. It shows how evaluating a program is itself a program.
aAlR3cezPJg.why: HN holds the SICP lectures up as joyful classics, and this lecture as the moment the evaluator is revealed.

aESqrP3hfi8.summary: Not Just Bikes explains why upright Dutch-style bicycles are comfortable and practical, and why they are rare outside the Netherlands.
aESqrP3hfi8.why: Cited in cycling and helmet discussions as the standard explanation of the Dutch bike and its safety benefits.

aYT2se94eU0.summary: Alan Kay's 1997 OOPSLA keynote argues that the computer revolution has not really happened yet, reflecting on how computing, objects and the web fall short of their potential.
aYT2se94eU0.why: HN regards it as a must-watch that gives a very different perspective on software and the web, and its title is widely riffed on.

ao2Jfm35XeE.summary: Veritasium visits snowflake expert Dr Ken Libbrecht, who grows designer snowflakes in the lab. The video explains how snowflakes form and why they take so many shapes.
ao2Jfm35XeE.why: Recommended as a fantastic, scientist-led explanation of snowflake formation.

a3ww0gwEszo.summary: Find the Longest Path is a comedic song by Daniel J. Barrett, a Billy Joel parody that describes the NP-hard longest path problem in informal terms.
a3ww0gwEszo.why: HN shares it as a fun, memorable way to explain the longest path problem and as an entry in lists of programming and math songs.

aFdpBqmDpzM.summary: An AWS re:Invent session explaining Amazon's Working Backwards process, where teams start from customer needs and write a press release and FAQ (PR-FAQ) before building. It covers the five customer questions that frame the process.
aFdpBqmDpzM.why: HN cites it as the primary source for Amazon's Working Backwards method whenever product-definition approaches come up.

aJ4TJ4-kkDw.summary: A short look at CoeLux, an artificial skylight that recreates the scattering process that makes the sky look blue, producing a convincing illusion of distant sun and depth.
aJ4TJ4-kkDw.why: HN points to it as a demonstration of artificial daylight, especially for windowless or underground rooms, and to date the technology to 2014.

aMkCKeZ8xZw.summary: Kees Cook of Google gives a Linux Foundation talk on the Kernel Self Protection Project, which aims to harden Linux against attackers. He surveys threats, the state of available defensive technologies and a year of community progress.
aMkCKeZ8xZw.why: Cited as the authoritative overview of kernel hardening goals and priorities, including Cook's car-safety analogy for kernel security.

aPvXnmBIO7o.summary: Thunderf00t debunks the Fontus self-filling water bottle, arguing that pulling meaningful amounts of water from air with a small solar-powered device is thermodynamically impractical.
aPvXnmBIO7o.why: Cited in atmospheric water harvesting threads as a debunking of products that promise drinking water from thin air.

aUgtMaAZzW0.summary: A 1993 Yoga Works video of the Ashtanga Yoga Primary Series led by Sri K. Pattabhi Jois, with senior students demonstrating. The class is filmed in classic style from the back of the room.
aUgtMaAZzW0.why: HN commenters suggest it as a free guided stretching routine, with the first half hour enough for a good stretch.

aVnRQRdePp4.summary: Engineer Sandy Munro joins an Autoline panel for a 100-minute deep dive on Tesla's design and manufacturing, including the Model 3 and its motors.
aVnRQRdePp4.why: HN links it as an expert teardown perspective on Tesla engineering, used to back up claims about motors and electronics quality.

a_TSR_v07m0.summary: Mark Rober spends eleven months building and testing a glitter bomb package with GPS and cameras to get back at porch pirates who steal parcels.
a_TSR_v07m0.why: HN brings it up as the obligatory link whenever package theft or booby-trapped parcels come up.

ab8GtuPdrUQ.summary: A one-minute clip from The IT Crowd in which the characters hear a jingle for a memorable emergency phone number.
ab8GtuPdrUQ.why: HN mostly invokes it as a joke in threads about emergency numbers and phone numbers.

abqAanC2NZs.summary: A demo of Brigade 3 real-time path tracing at 720p controlled with an Xbox controller. Depth of field, field of view, reflections and shadows can be altered live.
abqAanC2NZs.why: Cited as an early proof that real-time path tracing was feasible, years before it reached mainstream games.

agMrewRJTow.summary: Engineering Explained compares Lexus's steer-by-wire yoke on the RZ 450e with Tesla's yoke. It covers how steer-by-wire works and how variable steering ratios address the yoke's flaws.
agMrewRJTow.why: HN points to it to explain how steer-by-wire is implemented and why variable steering ratio is its benefit.

agxSclh27uo.summary: AdoredTV relays leaks and insider accounts of what it is like inside Intel, including staffing changes and morale. It is a commentary video from 2020.
agxSclh27uo.why: HN cites it as an insider account of Intel replacing senior staff with contractors, in threads about Intel's decline.

akvSE5Z474c.summary: A 1971 DEC LAB-8/e (PDP-8/e) minicomputer plays music by inducing noise into a nearby AM radio. The software is Richard Wilson's 1975 Music Compiler running under OS/8.
akvSE5Z474c.why: HN cites it as an early example of making a computer emit music over AM radio through electromagnetic side effects.

antLneVlxcs.summary: AI Addict films a Tesla FSD Beta 8.2 drive through Oakland, annotating close calls, disengagements, pedestrians and wrong-lane moments with timestamps.
antLneVlxcs.why: HN uses it as evidence of how rough Tesla's self-driving was in 2021, usually in skeptical threads.

aoag03mSuXQ.summary: Veritasium tells the story of the XZ backdoor, how a patient attacker became maintainer and nearly compromised SSH on Linux systems. It also covers free software history and how encryption in SSH works.
aoag03mSuXQ.why: Cited as an accessible, documentary-style account of the XZ backdoor in supply chain security discussions.

aolI_Rz0ZqY.summary: Scott Chacon's FOSDEM 2024 talk on lesser-known Git tips and tricks: useful config settings, older and newer commands, monorepo and big-repo features, and recent GitHub additions. It closes with why he is now building GitButler, followed by a Q&A.
aolI_Rz0ZqY.why: HN commenters point to it as a well-regarded tour of newer, lesser-known Git features, and it is among the most-watched engineering talks of 2024.

aqqEYz38ens.summary: CNLohr maps Wi-Fi signal strength at high resolution by moving an ESP8266 on a CNC mill, then visualizes the 3D data in WebGL. The result shows interference patterns in space.
aqqEYz38ens.why: Cited as a cool, concrete visualization of Wi-Fi interference patterns.

ar-poc38C84.summary: Short archival footage of a USMC KC-130F Hercules making unarrested landings and takeoffs on the USS Forrestal in 1963. It is the largest and heaviest aircraft to have landed on a carrier, and the tests were judged successful but too risky for routine use.
ar-poc38C84.why: HN commenters link it as the go-to example of what a carrier deck can handle and as an impressive flight feat.

aw6RsUhw1Q8.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on coal examines the industry, its executives and its treatment of miners, and includes the coverage of Robert Murray that led to a lawsuit.
aw6RsUhw1Q8.why: HN refers to it mainly for context on coal executive Robert Murray and the lawsuit that followed the segment.

awADEuv5vWY.summary: Inventor Mary Lou Jepsen demonstrates using red light and sound to see inside the body and brain, aiming at tumor detection and neural activity measurement, and potentially a cheaper wearable MRI replacement.
awADEuv5vWY.why: HN mentions it as a reference for Openwater's approach of light-based deep tissue imaging.

ay-gqx18UTM.summary: A short demo showing slow 2D drawing in the Windows 7 GUI compared with XP. It attributes the slowdown to the display driver model lacking hardware accelerated GDI.
ay-gqx18UTM.why: Used as the reference example when people argue Windows UI responsiveness regressed after XP.

ay2uwtRO3QE.summary: Uber Engineering's Joseph Gilley explains why Uber uses hexagons for geospatial indexing and introduces H3, its open source hierarchical grid system. He covers use cases and how distortion is handled.
ay2uwtRO3QE.why: HN points to it as the detailed explanation of why hexagons suit map grids, in threads about H3.

ayh0qebfD2g.summary: The 8-Bit Guy proposes building his dream retro computer, an expandable C64-like machine using sourceable parts and modern I/O, which became the Commander X16 project.
ayh0qebfD2g.why: HN points to it as the original proposal that explains the vision behind the Commander X16.

a0BpfwazhUA.summary: The People's Front of Judea scene from Monty Python's Life of Brian, a satire of squabbling revolutionary factions.
a0BpfwazhUA.why: HN invokes it as a joke about infighting among groups with nearly identical aims.

aCbfMkh940Q.summary: A clip from the film Aliens in which Ripley says to nuke the entire site from orbit because it is the only way to be sure.
aCbfMkh940Q.why: Posted as a joke reply wherever a drastic, scorched-earth solution fits.

aCgkLICTskQ.summary: Mark Fisher's 2014 talk in Zagreb on the slow cancellation of the future, about cultural stagnation and the sense that popular culture has stopped producing the new.
aCgkLICTskQ.why: Mentioned in threads about cultural stagnation as the obligatory related talk by Fisher.

aI0euMFAWF8.summary: A one-minute clip from a Simpsons episode showing Mr. Burns as indestructible despite his many ailments.
aI0euMFAWF8.why: HN uses it purely as a joke reply, for example about flu seasons, big contracts or vaccines.

aMli33ornEU.summary: A demo of Quake's E1M1 rendered as vector graphics on a Hitachi oscilloscope. A laptop generates the audio signal that the scope draws.
aMli33ornEU.why: Cited as the canonical example of Quake running on an exotic display, usually in 'will it run Doom' threads.

aNaXdLWt17A.summary: The Swamp Castle scene from Monty Python and the Holy Grail, where wedding plans go awry.
aNaXdLWt17A.why: Posted as a joke or comedic reference in threads where the situation resembles the skit.

aNi17YLnZpg.summary: A short clip of a Volvo C60 automatic braking demonstration in which the car fails to stop. It was widely circulated as a press-demo embarrassment.
aNi17YLnZpg.why: Cited as a cautionary example whenever collision-avoidance or self-driving safety systems come up.

aRrDsbUdY_k.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on credit reports, explaining their outsized role in people's lives and how often they contain critical errors.
aRrDsbUdY_k.why: Referenced as a quick, entertaining overview of problems with credit reporting and scoring.

aWejiXvd-P8.summary: A one-minute clip of Donald Trump at a 2015 Iowa event saying he would bomb ISIS. The uploader's description is openly supportive.
aWejiXvd-P8.why: Mentions are mostly critical or incidental references in political threads, not recommendations.

aWfYxg-Ypm4.summary: A short parody sketch of a job interview with a senior JavaScript developer, poking fun at the JS ecosystem and trendy stacks.
aWfYxg-Ypm4.why: HN uses it as a joke reference in threads about DevOps, cognitive load and rewrites to Node.js.

aXV-yaFmQNk.summary: A one-minute video of a baby treating a print magazine like a broken iPad, presented as a tribute to Steve Jobs. It makes a point about how touch screens shape the expectations of digital natives.
aXV-yaFmQNk.why: Cited as a humorous, somewhat contrived example of children and technology dependence.

aYbNh3NS7jA.summary: An open Q&A with Python creator Guido van Rossum hosted by Microsoft Reactor, covering his career, PyCon's origins and his opinions on other languages.
aYbNh3NS7jA.why: HN uses it as a source for Guido's views on Rust, Go and Python 4, with timestamps shared.

aZ2czFuIYmQ.summary: Benn Jordan measures air quality around vinyl records with a pollution meter and finds high particulate and VOC levels. He argues vinyl should be modernized.
aZ2czFuIYmQ.why: Cited as the source for claims that PVC records outgas harmful compounds, usually in vinyl revival threads.

a_Vy6fgaBPE.summary: Dr. Anthony Fauci joins the This Week in Virology podcast to discuss SARS-CoV-2 transmission, testing, immunity, vaccines and preparedness.
a_Vy6fgaBPE.why: Cited in debates over PCR cycle thresholds, as a place where Fauci addressed them directly.

aaOB-ErYq6Y.summary: Waymo's 2017 announcement that its fully autonomous vehicles are test-driving on public roads with no one in the driver's seat. It gives a short overview of the project's history and plans.
aaOB-ErYq6Y.why: Cited as evidence of Waymo's progress in Arizona and its lead over competitors.

abapFJN6glo.summary: A short animation that pairs the sound of a dialup modem handshake with a graphic explaining what each phase of the sound means.
abapFJN6glo.why: Shared in dial-up nostalgia threads as a way to both hear and understand the handshake.

acLW1vFO-2Q.summary: A three-minute excerpt from George Carlin's 2005 special Life Is Worth Losing, in which he riffs on the American Dream and the education system, ending that you have to be asleep to believe it.
acLW1vFO-2Q.why: Quoted as shorthand for cynicism about education and the American establishment.

ad_higXixRA.summary: On The Ellen Show, Bill Gates plays a game guessing the prices of grocery items.
ad_higXixRA.why: Linked to show that a billionaire's price guesses are reasonable, usually in threads about out-of-touch wealthy people.

ahgjEjJkZks.summary: A Yes, Prime Minister scene in which Sir Humphrey shows how leading questions can make a poll produce either answer on national service.
ahgjEjJkZks.why: Linked whenever surveys or polls are suspected of manipulation through question wording.

aqz-KE-bpKQ.summary: The 4K, 60fps version of Big Buck Bunny, the Creative Commons-licensed animated short film from the Blender Foundation.
aqz-KE-bpKQ.why: Used as a freely licensed sample video for demoing multimedia tools, and as a test file in discussions of video downloading and playback.

arMH5GjBwUQ.summary: Gerald Jay Sussman speaks at Dan Friedman's 60th birthday celebration about how programming helps formulate and clarify ideas. He argues that ambiguous mathematical notation hinders understanding.
arMH5GjBwUQ.why: Cited for Sussman's argument that programs make ideas precise in a way standard math notation does not.

arss9V3A1VA.summary: Phone footage of looting in the makeup aisle of a San Francisco CVS, with commentary that police did not show.
arss9V3A1VA.why: Cited in threads about San Francisco shoplifting and crime policy as an example of brazen theft.

asUyK6JWt9U.summary: A Not the Nine O'Clock News sketch that satirizes the controversy around Monty Python's Life of Brian.
asUyK6JWt9U.why: Mentioned as the sketch many Britons remember in discussions of the Life of Brian controversy.

av9Xi6CNqq4.summary: Anthony Marcar describes lessons from three years of using Clojure at WalmartLabs, including scaling a team and a large multi-project codebase in an enterprise setting.
av9Xi6CNqq4.why: HN cites it as evidence of Clojure running real large-scale production systems at Walmart and as a behind-the-scenes talk from that team.

azEvfD4C6ow.summary: A short, absurd happy-hardcore song and animation celebrating the Bagger 288, the enormous bucket-wheel excavator, in dramatic over-the-top terms.
azEvfD4C6ow.why: HN mostly drops it as a joke whenever giant machines or huge ships and excavators come up.
